title: about 23 km apart
text: They grew up in neighbouring towns in central Alberta, Clayton in Red Deer and Gordon in Lacombe, on the same rail line and less than half an hour apart. Gordon was six years older. No record shows whether they knew each other then.

title: about 5 km apart, going by his brigade
text: The closest they came in the war. On July 20, 1944, Clayton's K troop was destroyed at Ifs, at the foot of Verrières Ridge. The attack Clayton's troop was supporting had tanks of the Sherbrooke Fusiliers, one of the three regiments of Gordon's 2nd Canadian Armoured Brigade, and their headquarters tanks sat in the orchard on the west side of Ifs. Gordon's field ambulance was that brigade's medical unit, so it was likely somewhere behind them, though nothing in his own records places him at Ifs. Whether any of Clayton's troop passed through Gordon's unit isn't recorded.

title: the same battle
text: In Operation Totalize, the night attack south from Caen on Aug. 7 and 8, 1944, the tanks of Gordon's brigade went in with Clayton's 2nd Division. Clayton's J troop was in close fighting at Fontenay-le-Marmion on Aug. 8. Both units then pushed on toward Falaise.

title: about 18 km apart
text: Late August 1944: Clayton's division fought through the forest south of Rouen and crossed at Elbeuf, while Gordon's brigade crossed the Seine nearby on Aug. 28.

title: within about 25 km
text: February and March 1945: both were in First Canadian Army's push through the Reichswald and Hochwald into Germany, around Cleve.

title: the same crossing, a day apart
text: Clayton's 23rd Battery crossed the Rhine at Rees at 11 p.m. on March 28, 1945, the first of his regiment across. Gordon's brigade crossed at Rees on March 29.

title: the same town
text: After the war both made their lives in Lacombe, Gordon running Sweet's Pharmacy and Clayton raising his family a few streets away. Their children later married.
